descriptionChirho: The core abstract sense of might, power, or strength as a quality or attribute of God, a king, or a person; rendered consistently as Arabic جَبَرُوت or قُوَّة, Korean 능력/힘, Hindi शक्ति/सामर्थ्य, and Swahili nguvu/uweza.

Concrete acts or manifestations of divine or royal power, typically in plural construct forms (גְּבוּרוֹת); rendered as Spanish proezas/hazañas, Korean 능력들, Swahili matendo makuu (great deeds), and Hindi पराक्रमों (feats of prowess).

Heroic courage, bravery, or martial prowess in a warfare context; distinguished from general might by Arabic بَأْس/بَطْش, Korean 용맹/용력/용기 (valor/prowess/courage), Hindi वीरता/शूरवीरता (heroism/warrior valor), and Swahili ushujaa (bravery).

By metonymy, the abstract quality standing for the people who possess it — warriors or champions; rendered as Arabic أَبطَال (champions), Korean 용사들 (warriors), Swahili mashujaa (warriors), and Hindi वीर (heroes).

The outcome or result of exercising might — victory, overcoming, or triumph; uniquely rendered as Arabic غَلَبَة (victory), Spanish victoria, Swahili ushindi (victory), and Korean 강함 (strength/prevailing).
